predecessors.name: Saadi Sultanate
predecessors.text: Salé and the Kasbah of Rabat at the mouth of the Bou Regreg, where 'the Hornacheros expelled the Sherif's governor'

successors.name: Morocco
successors.text: Salé and Rabat on the Bou Regreg: Moulay al-Rashid 'ended the republic's independence' in June 1668

capitals.name: Kasbah of the Oudayas (Rabat) and Salé

ledger.x: April 1627: the Hornacheros of Rabat and Salé form a corsair republic.
June 1668: Moulay al-Rashid ends the republic.

wars.name: Hornacheros' coup at Salé
wars.outcome: The Hornacheros expelled the Sherif's governor in April 1627 and made themselves a virtually independent republic; John Harrison negotiated a treaty with Sidi al-Ayachi in May.

wars.name: Civil strife between Andalusians and Hornacheros
wars.outcome: Clashes ended in 1630 with a 16-member Diwan split between Andalusians and Hornacheros; fighting resumed in 1636-1637 and English ships bombarded the Kasbah in 1637; in 1631 the Hornacheros sent a draft treaty offering the city to Philip IV's monarchy.

wars.name: Dila'iya hegemony over Salé
wars.outcome: In 1641 the Zawiya Dila'iya 'imposed a religious hegemony over Salé and its parent republic'; the infobox has the republic under Dila'iya suzerainty 1641-1661; Salé rose against the Dila'ite governor in 1660 and was lost to the Zawiya in 1661 (Dila page); the…

wars.name: Alawite conquest of the Bou Regreg
wars.outcome: Moulay al-Rashid defeated the Dilaites in June 1668 and ended the republic's independence; Salé 'acknowledged his authority'.

certainty.note: A walled city state: the two cities on the Bou Regreg are the whole territory; no outer frontier exists.
